newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. ballistic missile team arrives in Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: U.N. ballistic missile team arrives in Baghdad.

text.p: U.N. ballistic missile experts arrived in Baghdad on Monday, the second team in a week to visit, a U.N. arms official said.
Jo Lomas, special assistant to the director of the Baghdad Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre, said the 13 experts intended to stay until August 26.
Lomas said their mission was different from that of another team which had been in Iraq since last Monday.
"The task that they will do is different but related to the missile (weapons), Lomas told Reuters.
Checking for banned missiles is among unresolved issues between Iraq and the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) charged with disarming it under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire conditions.
UNSCOM has not yet made public the results of its analysis of about 100 Iraqi missiles it sent to laboratories in the United States and France last April.

Under the ceasefire terms, Iraq is not allowed to keep or produce missiles with ranges greater than 150 km (90 miles) or the means to produce them. UNSCOM has said it still cannot ascertain that Baghdad does not keep any such missiles.
Lomas said the new team would also carry out inspections.

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, although Baghdad is allowed limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
